newsitem.title: UK: Stg junk bond to fund BBC transmission sale - paper.
newsitem.headline: Stg junk bond to fund BBC transmission sale - paper.

text.p: Credit Suisse First Boston and J.P. Morgan are preparing to underwrite the first sterling-denominated junk bond to fund the acquisition of the BBC's transmission network, the Evening Standard newspaper said on Thursday.

A 100 million stg bond is expected for Castle Transmission Services, a U.S.-led consortium which bought the BBC's domestic radio and television transmission network for around 250 million stg last February, the paper said.
Roadshows for the bonds are expected to start next week, the Evening Standard said.
Officials at CSFB and J.P. Morgan were not immediately available for comment.
The first European junk bonds were issued in April when two companies launched mark-denominated deals, the first non-dollar transactions.
Junk bonds, issued by unrated or low-rated companies, provide investors with a substantial yield pick-up over more conventional bonds launched by highly-rated banks and companies.
European investors are turning to high-risk company debt in an effort to boost returns on their portfolios in a low-inflation, low-interest rate environment.
Some bankers estimate the European junk bond market could total up to $30 billion equivalent per year over time. The sector is well-established in the U.S., with around $210 billion outstanding.
